newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jews hail Swiss holocaust foundation move.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jews hail Swiss holocaust foundation move.

text.p: Jewish leaders on Wednesday hailed Switzerland's creation of a Jewish-Swiss humanitarian fund for Holocaust victims as historic and a New York state official lifted a ban on putting state funds in Swiss banks.
World Jewish Congress President Edgar Bronfman, whose group negotiated details of the fund with the Swiss, said it was an "historic turning point in Swiss-Jewish relations."

Bronfman, who is also the president of the World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO), added: "I believe this marks an honest confrontation and writing the last chapter of a terrible period of the Second World War."
Because of the agreement on the fund, the WJC said that New York State Comptroller Carl McCall had lifted his ban on making short-term deposits of state funds in Swiss banks.
McCall imposed the ban last month after expressing dissatisfaction with Switzerland's slowness in getting a fund established.
He lifted the ban shortly before the three major Swiss banks got the fund started with a donation of $68 million.
The Swiss government announced on Wednesday that the fund will be jointly administered by Swiss and Jewish representatives from the WJRO.
Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti said the Federal Council, or cabinet, approved a decree setting up the fund on March 1.
The decree sets up a board of seven directors, four of them "eminent personalities" from Switzerland and three to be named by the WJRO.
"The Federal Council will have overall supervision of the fund," the decree said.
